pretreatments.description: Microwave Pretreatment (MP) was applied to green marine macroalgae substrates using an electromagnetic field. It involved liquefaction of the biomass in 500 mL polytetrafluoroethylene sealed containers with a 1:50 substrate to water ratio. The process was performed using a microwave oven (IFB-30SC2) at varying powers ranging from 90 W to 720 W (optimal at 450 W) and treatment times from 1 to 60 minutes (optimal at 15 minutes). Microwave conditions were characterized by a higher power and frequency of 900 W and 2450 MHz respectively, utilizing thermal and dielectric effects to disintegrate cell walls and enhance liquefaction efficiency.

Surfactant Microwave Pretreatment (SMP) was applied by combining MP with sodium dodecylbenzene sulfonate (SDBS) as a surfactant to enhance organic release. The SMP process utilized a similar 1:50 substrate to water ratio (500 mL container) at optimal MP conditions but varied SDBS concentration from 0.005 to 0.5 g/g TS to 0.04 g/g TS for the optimal dosage, where protein, carbohydrate, and lipid release was maximized. This combined pretreatment minimized specific energy input and loss of organics associated with MP, leading to increased liquefaction rates and bio-precursors release suitable for anaerobic fermentation.
